description: Lab records with total cholesterol equal to 180 count as passing the filter (T-CHO at least 180).

b.request: For laboratory records joined to patients on ID, keep records with `T-CHO` ≥ 180, group by each distinct recorded `SEX` value including blank, and report `SEX`, the unrounded average of nonmissing `Laboratory.DNA` values, and the unrounded average of `ALB` − `TP` where both values are present, leaving either average empty when no values qualify.
b.sql: SELECT p.SEX, AVG(CASE WHEN NULLIF(TRIM(l.DNA), '') IS NOT NULL THEN CAST(l.DNA AS REAL) END) AS avg_DNA, AVG(CASE WHEN l.ALB IS NOT NULL AND l.TP IS NOT NULL THEN l.ALB - l.TP END) AS avg_ALB_minus_TP FROM Laboratory AS l JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE l.`T-CHO` >= 180 GROUP BY p.SEX
b.raw: For laboratory records joined to patients on ID, keep records with `T-CHO` ≥ 180, group by each distinct recorded `SEX` value including blank, and report `SEX`, the unrounded average of nonmissing `Laboratory.DNA` values, and the unrounded average of `ALB` − `TP` where both values are present, leaving either average empty when no values qualify.

a.request: For lab records that match a patient by ID (unmatched records dropped) and have total cholesterol (`T-CHO`) of 180 or higher, break them down by patient sex (`SEX`), keeping each recorded value, including a blank one, as its own group. For each group, show the sex, the average anti-DNA level (`Laboratory.DNA`), and the average of albumin minus total protein (`ALB` − `TP`), ignoring missing values and leaving the average empty if there are none, unrounded.
a.sql: SELECT p.SEX, AVG(CAST(NULLIF(TRIM(l.DNA), '') AS REAL)) AS average_anti_dna, AVG(l.ALB - l.TP) AS average_albumin_minus_total_protein FROM Laboratory AS l JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE l.`T-CHO` >= 180 GROUP BY p.SEX

c.request: For lab records that match a patient by ID (unmatched records dropped), screened with 180 as the total cholesterol (`T-CHO`) cutoff, break them down by patient sex (`SEX`), keeping each recorded value, including a blank one, as its own group. For each group, show the sex, the average anti-DNA level (`Laboratory.DNA`), and the average of albumin minus total protein (`ALB` − `TP`), ignoring missing values and leaving the average empty if there are none, unrounded. Lab records with total cholesterol equal to 180 count as passing the filter (T-CHO at least 180).
c.sql: SELECT p.SEX, AVG(NULLIF(TRIM(l.DNA), '')) AS average_anti_dna, AVG(l.ALB - l.TP) AS average_albumin_minus_total_protein FROM Laboratory AS l INNER JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE l.`T-CHO` >= 180 GROUP BY p.SEX

d.request: For laboratory records with `T-CHO` ≥ 180 that match a patient by `ID`, group by each recorded `Patient.SEX` value, including blank values, and return the sex, the unrounded average of nonmissing `Laboratory.DNA` values, and the unrounded average of `ALB` − `TP` where both values are present; leave an average empty when its group has no qualifying values.
d.sql: SELECT p.SEX AS sex, AVG(NULLIF(TRIM(l.DNA), '')) AS avg_dna, AVG(l.ALB - l.TP) AS avg_alb_minus_tp FROM Laboratory AS l JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE l.`T-CHO` >= 180 GROUP BY p.SEX
